touches.text: Outline check: when a ticket is cast, the cheapest model reads it beside the outline sections it touches. A conflict, or an open question in those sections, becomes a [Q#n] at the outline line it bears on (0.6.2), and that open [Q#n] holds the ticket's build until it is answered. It reads the outline as it stands each time, so editing the outline costs nothing. WHY: a ticket that contradicts the outline builds something Akien did not intend, and the cheapest time to catch that is before the build. - CC

A ticket's plan carries only what a door can check. A decision line's by (free prose on every ticket) is not checked and not kept: the cast door checks writes_to and reads, and by goes. Who authored a line is not tracked, except on a gate-pass certificate. WHY: tickets moved from prose to JSON so their contents can be checked; a field no door checks is prose. - CC
Owns the inspectors and gates (9.4): everything in the code pipeline that checks. The exception is diagnostic_inspector, which is base's (17.1).

Commit: the proofs of the component the ticket changed, since RULE 1 bounds a change to its component. Passing them puts the component in service, yellow: proven where it changed, not yet measured against what depends on it. In service needs only the best we can do now: 80% trust.

A seal is host independent: one record per proof, whichever box asks. Seals are made by one sealing machine in the cairn device, and there is only ever one cairn (until a laptop dies and a backup takes over), so there is one sealer. A box that is not cairn's home asks the sealer instead of writing its own seal.

A choice CC can answer is not a question; it is a hypothesis. The ticket carries CC's answer as its hypothesis, and its WATCHME feeds the hypothesis back to cc_0 with enough data to review it and rewrite it as we learn. The notation carries the question: a HYPOTHESIS asks whether it works, or is faster, or whatever it claims, and the WATCHME answers that. A question asks only what Akien alone can settle. Why? Because a question with a recommendation asks him to adjudicate what a measurement can settle. This holds everywhere. - CC
Akien's head is the spec: what the system should be. Every artifact, these files included, is a translation of it. Why? Becuase it's the best we've come up with so far.

CC (any CC session) writes readings: its translation of what he means, and the specific contents of the tools he designed (17.11.6.1). Why? This allows us to start exploring clearly marking the boundary between what claude has decided and what akien has decided so akien is not the first consultee if he didn't make the mark.

Prebuild face: the chart chain, eight machines, each answering one question before a build begins: orient (what is asked, where does it live), constrain (what bounds it), survey (what already exists), decompose (how does it split), triage (what first, by what standard), hypothesize (what do we expect, how would we know we're wrong), validate (what does DONE mean, measured), and after the build, verdict (what done actually meant).

Each stage moves from the model to deterministic code once a proof a hollow build could not pass can hold it; hypothesize stays with the model longest. Validate sends a local miss back to hypothesize and a structural one back to design. A build that finds new work spawns children that enter at decompose.

How the TESTING database works. (1) The db proxy is the seam (4.3.1.5.1.4.1.1, 11.3.7): proofs, devices and tools never choose a database; the proxy chooses by session context. (2) The test runner sets the context, never the proof: bin/cairn test and the hollow run open every db session with context=testing, so a proof can neither forget it nor pick live (Law 4). (3) In testing context, writes go only to the TESTING database: same schema, rows from a reserved address range, so a testing address never collides with a live one. (4) In testing context, reads are an overlay: testing rows first, live underneath, live pinned at the seq the run started at. A proof reads live with no fixtures, what it wrote shadows live for that run only, and the run repeats within itself. (5) In live context the proxy never consults the TESTING database, so testing artifacts are invisible to all but the run that made them, by construction rather than by filtering. (6) Each run's testing rows carry its run id and are dropped at run end; the sleep cycle sweeps orphans. (7) A proof over live data asserts invariants, never snapshots; a tooth that needs an exact value writes its fixture into the overlay first. Until the per-box proxy exists, the same routing sits in the store door (db_domain) and moves into the proxy when it is built. WHY: a context the proof sets is a context a proof can forget; the runner is the one place every proof passes through. - akiendelllinux_orchestrator -amm
